title: Reunion Special Goes to Philly: Gibbs Runs Over the Dawgs While Kai's Best Players Watch From the Bench
dek: Team Pillbert wins its fourth straight in the Jeanty-and-Adams grudge match, JMoney finally gets in the win column, and three teams now share first place at 4-1 heading into a Horse-versus-HULK showdown.
body: The game everybody circled went to the guy who started the whole thing. Team Pillbert beat Mekhi's Dawgs 143.66 to 108.44, and Jahmyr Gibbs was the wrecking ball, posting 35.2 points on a 24.57 projection, the top score of the week. Justin Jefferson put up 15.8 in his first game in Pillbert colors, while the two players Alan shipped out for him, Davante Adams and Ashton Jeanty, gave Kai 19.6 and 9.2 against their old boss. The departed duo outscored the new arrival, and Philly still won by 35. That's four straight wins and a 4-1 record for Team Pillbert.

The painful part for Mekhi is that he had the firepower to make this a game and left it in the dugout. Tyler Shough started at quarterback and scored -0.16 on a 16.51 projection, while Jayden Daniels sat on the bench with 32.26. Swapping those two alone would have closed all but 2.8 points of the gap, and Christian Watson was also on the bench with 29.3 on an 11.52 projection. That's 61.56 points from two benchwarmers, nearly double the final margin. Kai is now 1-4, and he went back to work on the wire, adding Malik Nabers for TreVeyon Henderson, swapping the Ravens D/ST for the Bengals and trading kicker Harrison Mevis for Will Reichard.

Ramon's No Banner only HULK took care of Randy's The fumblers 134 to 99.64 as a 63% favorite, and Josh Allen led the way with 30.5 points. Brucie also had Matthew Stafford's 27.32 on the bench and didn't need it, which is the kind of problem only the best team in the league gets to have. In a related development, the Bills fan dropped the Bills D/ST for T.J. Hockenson, so loyalty has its limits. The HULK's title odds jumped from 41% to 55%, and its 695 points for are now 70.5 clear of anyone else.

Randy got a monster game from Jaylen Warren, 33.8 points on a 15.86 projection, and it went to waste. The fumblers have now lost two straight, and their title odds cratered from 14% to 4%, with playoff odds at a coin-flip 48%. Randy's week on the waiver wire was a story of its own: he dropped Trevor Lawrence for Deshaun Watson, then dropped Watson and picked Lawrence back up, a full lap around the quarterback market that ended exactly where it started. He also cut Courtland Sutton, added Romeo Doubs, swapped the Rams D/ST for the Raiders and replaced kicker Tyler Loop with Matt Gay.

JMoney is on the board. Counting or not Counting GV beat Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN 119.68 to 69.14 as a 43% underdog, and the new guy did the heavy lifting: Isaiah Likely scored 26.9 in his debut, just a week after Jordan got him in the Jeanty deal. The other two pieces of that trade, Emeka Egbuka (14.2) and Denzel Boston (12.1), scored from the bench, and Jeremiyah Love's 2.2 on a 13.06 projection kept it from being a bigger blowout. For Z², Jared Goff was terrific with 28.94, but the rest of the lineup combined for 40.2, and a week after knocking off Sonny she's back to 2-3 with 10% playoff odds.

Sonny's The Horse is Hea won 137.6 to 118.34 at the Habibsters, powered by Bucky Irving's 30.5 points on a 13.97 projection. Tony Pollard didn't even last a week on the roster; Sonny swapped him for Emanuel Wilson. Habib got 29.2 from Puka Nacua, but CeeDee Lamb went from 32.8 last week to 1.9 on a 15.46 projection, and that swing was most of the ballgame. Kaushal is 1-4 with 577.4 points for, the fourth-most in the league and more than 3-2 Randy, which is why the model still gives him 30% playoff odds, better than the 2-3 team above him.

And Philly isn't done shopping. Alan made his third trade in roughly a week, sending George Pickens and Ollie Gordon II to Sonny for Chuba Hubbard and DeVonta Smith. That means Hubbard leaves The Horse is Hea having scored 25.4 points as a Horse and exactly zero of them in a starting lineup. Team Pillbert also added and dropped Joe Mixon in the same week and picked up Keon Coleman and Odell Beckham Jr. Despite the four-game win streak, Pillbert's title odds slipped from 21% to 16%, so the model remains unconvinced by all the remodeling.

The top of the table is now a three-way tie at 4-1: No Banner only HULK, Team Pillbert and The Horse is Hea, with Sonny's title odds climbing from 11% to 18% to edge past Philly. Week 6 brings the heavyweight bout, as the Horse hosts the HULK with first place on the line. Alan gets Randy, which means Javonte Williams lines up against the manager who traded him away, and Randy badly needs a win to stop the slide. Zoe faces Kai in a battle of teams that need to start stacking wins now, and Habib hosts JMoney in a game the points-rich Habibsters cannot afford to lose.

trade_watch.take: Round one of the production battle went to Kai: Adams and Jeanty combined for 28.8 in his lineup to Jefferson's 15.8, a 13-point edge. But Philly won the actual game by 35, so the scoreboard and the box score are telling two different stories.
This one already looks like JMoney's. Likely scored 26.9 in a win, Egbuka and Boston added 26.3 more from the bench, and Alan got nothing out of Jeanty because he'd already flipped him to Mekhi.
Stefon Diggs didn't play this week, so Randy got nothing from that side, while Javonte Williams added 13.2 for Philly. The gap is now 42 to 6, and Randy faces Williams head-on in week 6.

Hubbard and Rice were both on bye, but the bigger news is that Sonny just traded Hubbard to Alan. He leaves the Horse with 25.4 points, zero of them in the lineup, while Rice still hasn't scored for Brucie.

bios.1: Back to 4-1 after Bucky Irving's 30.5 beat the Habibsters, with title odds up from 11% to 18%. Sonny flipped Chuba Hubbard to Alan for George Pickens and Ollie Gordon II and now hosts the HULK with first place on the line.
bios.2: Two straight losses have dropped Randy to 3-2, with title odds collapsing from 14% to 4% and playoff odds at 48%. Jaylen Warren's 33.8 went to waste, and a busy week on the wire ended with the same quarterback he started with.
bios.3: Finally in the win column, as Isaiah Likely's 26.9-point debut powered a 50-point rout of Ghostu-Spider SZN. JMoney is 1-4 with 1% playoff odds, but his trade haul is already making him a tougher out.
bios.4: Four straight wins and a 4-1 record, highlighted by Jahmyr Gibbs' 35.2 against the team Alan just traded with. Philly has rebuilt his roster through three trades in about a week, but the model has trimmed his title odds to 16% anyway.
bios.5: Kai is 1-4 after a loss in which Jayden Daniels and Christian Watson combined for 61.56 points on his bench. Adams and Jeanty delivered in their debut, and the addition of Malik Nabers keeps a 25% playoff chance alive.
bios.6: The unluckiest 1-4 team imaginable, with the fourth-most points in the league and 30% playoff odds to show for it. Puka Nacua delivered 29.2, but CeeDee Lamb's 1.9 sank Habib against the Horse.
bios.7: The league's best team by a distance: 4-1, 695 points for and title odds up to 55% after Josh Allen's 30.5 sank The fumblers. Ramon left Stafford's 27.32 on the bench and still won by 34, and next up is a first-place showdown with The Horse is Hea.
bios.8: Zoe's team hit a wall at 69.14 points despite Jared Goff's 28.94, falling to 2-3 a week after upsetting the Horse. Playoff odds sit at 10%, and a week 6 date with the Dawgs is close to a must-win.
